messages:
anna: heads up — after last deploy small charts (sparklines/mini-heatmaps) are hanging ~300-400ms on first paint.
ben: saw the same in telemetry. main-thread parse and scriptEvaluate spiked right after rollout.
anna: stack traces point at a newly combined shared chunk (ui-utils) that jumped from ~120KB -> ~450KB.
kai: along with that, yesterday's routing policy tweak lowered weight for /widgets/sparkline so prefetches are being deprioritized.
lina: if prefetchs run on low-priority pool the kv/prefix cache won't warm, so first render pulls the big chunk and parses.
anna: quick evidence from canary logs:
```
grep "splitpoint ui-utils" -n canary-logs | tail -n 20
# repeated: GET /static/chunks/ui-utils.* 200
# script evaluate ~0.35s
```
ben: @kai can you confirm the routing weight change? that would explain why the prefetch work gets scheduled late.
kai: confirmed — /widgets/sparkline routing weight went 0.10 -> 0.02 in the rollout at 1717100000. quotas kicked in and prefetch tasks got pushed back.
lina: short-term mitigation: add a routeHint on prefetch for these widgets so they target the guaranteed pool, or bump prefetch priority: `prefetch: { routeHint: "fast", priority: "high" }`.
ben: longer-term: either revert the ui-utils aggregation (so tree-shaking reduces size) or split the chunk more aggressively for critical small widgets.
anna: i'm going to roll a canary that pins sparklines to the guaranteed pool until we fix the bundle split. low-risk revert.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/eng-platform-sparkline-pin -> eng-platform-canary-1. Rollback available via /deploy rollback <id>.
kai: i'll follow up with telemetry dashboards to track kvcache hits and parse durations once canary is live.
anna: thanks — i'll open a short triage doc with steps: revert vs chunk-split experiment, telemetry queries, and a perf regression checklist. :thumbsup:
